category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.recovery_moves = ['Use top-down photos.', 'Drill bird\'s eye.', 'Compare side vs top views.'] — concrete but does not branch by diagnostic, and the trap is not anchored to named research on spatial reasoning development.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite Battista (spatial reasoning) or Liben & Downs (children's mapping/perspective-taking research) by name in the rationale, and branch recovery_moves: if child can articulate 'above' but draws side view, do the drone-photo overlay; if child cannot conceive of bird's-eye view at all, drop back to physically standing on a chair to look down at a desk, then trace the footprint onto paper before re-attempting the map.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: differentiation block lists for_emerging/for_extending/for_ell_or_iep/for_movement_learners but provides NO no-paper, no-purchase alternative path. lesson_specific_materials still requires 'Map Template (1 per pair)' and 'Map Symbol Cards (12)' for the action stations.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit no-materials version to differentiation: e.g., 'No-paper version — children walk a small zone of the classroom and SAY their map aloud ("From the door, I see a square desk on my left, then a circle carpet, then a long rectangle bookshelf"). Use chalk on the floor or fingers traced on a partner's back as the bird's-eye sketch.' This makes Lesson 4 runnable on a day when no template was photocopied.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names the side-view-vs-top-down trap but does not invite children to invent or compare mapping strategies, and does not cite the spatial-reasoning research base (Battista, Liben & Downs, NRC 'Learning to Think Spatially').
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a strategy-comparison move in the action: have two pairs share their bedroom maps and compare how they chose symbols — 'Sam drew the bed as a rectangle; Priya drew it as a rectangle with a pillow circle. Which symbol is easier for a reader? Why?' Then in expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the misconception in research terms (Liben & Downs: children's developing understanding of representational correspondence on maps; or Battista on the projective-to-orthographic shift).

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet Parts 2 and 3 (map bedroom; map a place at home) are near-rote repeats of lesson Action Stations B and C. The worksheet does not deliberately VARY format with a transfer task or include 2 unfamiliar items to verify generalization. Part 1's pre-built map (bed, desk, door, window) duplicates the bedroom items children just mapped in the lesson rather than introducing novel objects.
category_feedback.required_fix: Vary Part 1: replace the bedroom pre-built map with a NEW context (e.g., a kitchen or library top-down) so children must transfer the read-symbols skill to unfamiliar items. Add a deliberate stretch in Part 3: 'Include at least 2 objects you did NOT map in class (e.g., a pet bed, a bookshelf, a rug)' and note the transfer rationale in worksheet teacher_notes. Justify the variation explicitly.
